state.incidentInput: Support says customers were charged but have no order.
state.summary: CFG-502 (inventory DB_POOL_MAX 20->80 at 13:52) overcommitted orders-db (budget 610 vs max 400), exhausting connections (397/400, LOG-076) so orders-service could not create orders after payment authorization. Payments confirms the 14 affected customers have duplicate holds, not completed captures, which auto-release in 3-5 days (USER-001). The cause is still the likely one and not confirmed by the change owner. Recovery not yet verified.
state.impact: Onset 13:55. Checkout 5xx up to 7.9%, orders error up to 10.3%; 87 tickets by 14:30 (CUST-001). 14 customers report being charged with no order (CUST-002); payments confirms these are duplicate holds that auto-release in 3-5 days (USER-001). Customers may see held funds for days. All regions (CUST-005).

hypotheses.statement: CFG-502 raised inventory pool to 80 x6 replicas, exhausting orders-db connections; orders-service failed to create orders after payment auth, leaving holds
hypotheses.reasoning: Timing and connection snapshots fit; USER-001 shows the customer harm is holds from auth without order, consistent with order creation failing. Not human-confirmed.

Can the holds be released early? (payments)

Ask payments whether to release them early
Re-enable payments_retry_on_timeout only after recovery verified
Deploy PgBouncer in front of orders-db

state.stakeholderUpdate: Some customers saw checkout errors, and 14 reported being charged without an order. Payments confirms these are temporary holds, not completed charges, and they release automatically in 3-5 days. The likely cause is a settings change that let one service use too many database connections, blocking order creation. We are reverting that setting. Next update in 30 minutes.

similarIncidents.lesson: 30 minutes lost investigating the most recent deploy rather than recent config changes.
